But over the past year, thanks to their viral bluegrass-drenched hit “Tennessee,” they’ve checked off several bucket list performances, including performing at Nashville’s Ryman Auditorium and Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, and making their Grand Ole Opry debut. “If you would’ve told us that when we were in Pat’s Snack Bar in Manchester, Kentucky, that we would play the Grand Ole Opry in two years, I’d probably say, ‘Give me what you’re drinking,’” quips Hacker. “That was a special moment for us to be able to share that with people we love and play the holy grail of country stages,” adds Horton. title: Rick Ross Gets Felony Domestic Violence Charge Dropped, Now Facing Only Misdemeanor
summary: The rapper was arrested earlier this month for allegedly striking his live-in girlfriend. Defense attorneys say he’s being “wrongfully accused.”
body: Rick Ross scored a legal win this week as Florida prosecutors dropped the most severe charge in his domestic violence case. The rapper was arrested on Oct. 1 and charged with battery by strangulation, a felony that can carry up to five years in prison, as well as misdemeanor battery. But in a Thursday (Oct. 29) court filing, obtained by Billboard , Miami prosecutors said they have “insufficient evidence” for that felony charge and will instead move forward only with the misdemeanor. That count carries a shorter maximum jail sentence of one year if convicted. title: YouTube bug keeps kicking viewers out of full screen and killing audio
summary: YouTube's mini-player goes rogue.
body: TL;DR Some YouTube users are reporting a bug that randomly kicks videos out of full-screen mode and into the floating mini player. The glitch also kills audio playback, forcing users to restart videos or the YouTube app to restore sound. Common troubleshooting steps haven’t helped. We’ve contacted Google to ask whether a fix is in the works. Despite its never-ending battle against ad blockers , YouTube otherwise offers a mostly fuss-free video streaming experience, especially if you’re a Premium subscriber. You open the app, scroll and find something you want to watch, and hit play. But what if even that seamless experience starts showing signs of instability? That’s precisely what some YouTube users, on both Android and iOS, are experiencing right now.

title: Not hearing your notifications on Android Auto? You’re not alone
summary: An Android Auto bug may have broken audio for notifications.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR An Android Auto bug is silencing notifications for some users. A pop-up will appear on the screen, but no sound will play through the vehicle’s speakers. The issue seems to be happening on devices running Android 17 and Android Auto 17.9 or newer. We learned this week that Android Auto could soon remember a preferred phone number for contacts with multiple numbers. While those changes have yet to roll out, a bug appears to have caused the platform to forget something else. Specifically, how to play a sound when a notification comes in. Some users are reporting that a glitch is causing notifications to be silenced on Android Auto. While a pop-up will still be shown on the screen, there’s no audio accompanying the alert. However, Android Auto reportedly pauses music as if it is trying to play the notification sound through the vehicle’s speakers.

title: Your favorite YouTube channel could suddenly appear blank — here’s why
summary: The new experiment could leave you subscribed to channels with nothing to watch.
body: TL;DR YouTube is testing a new cleanup process that gives certain channels facing termination over spam violations a second chance. Eligible creators have 30 days to fix or remove offending videos, or delete their entire video library to avoid termination. Creators who wipe their videos can retain their subscribers, channel handle, and monetization status, potentially leaving viewers with empty channels in their subscriptions. Preview Imagine heading to YouTube to revisit an old video from one of your favorite creators, only to find that the video, and in some cases, the creator’s entire library, has vanished. You’d normally blame YouTube, but soon, the platform might not be the culprit. The streaming giant is testing a new approach to dealing with channels that violate certain spam policies, and it includes giving creators the chance to voluntarily delete videos to save their channel from being terminated .

title: Android’s SMS of Death bug can knock out your phone, but a fix is coming soon
summary: Even emergency calls aren't safe from this silent threat.
body: TL;DR A newly disclosed Android vulnerability allows malicious text messages to silently crash a phone’s calling service, potentially interrupting emergency calls. Repeated messages can trigger persistent crashes and reboot loops, making affected devices hard to recover without technical help. Google developed a fix months before the public disclosure, but questions remain about when users will receive the patch. Imagine dialing 911, only for your phone to suddenly drop the call . You haven’t pressed anything, your signal hasn’t disappeared, and there’s no obvious explanation. Somewhere in the background, however, a text message you never received has just brought your phone’s calling service to its knees. That’s the frightening scenario behind SMS of Death , a newly disclosed Android vulnerability that lets attackers remotely disrupt phones without the victim lifting a finger.

title: I tested the 7 most popular Android launchers — here’s my ranking
summary: One launcher clearly beats out the rest.
body: Default launchers from Google, Samsung, and Motorola have admittedly gotten more feature-rich and pleasing to the eye in recent years. However, they still implement some restrictions to prevent users from straying too far from their signature aesthetics. For example, you can’t remove the Google Search bar from the Pixel UI home screen. Similarly, you can’t replace the Google News app on the left of the homepage. The same goes for the default launchers of Samsung and Motorola. You’re only allowed to turn off Google’s News app completely and lose that virtual real estate.

title: iPhone Duo’s cracking screens are already scaring off would-be buyers, survey finds
summary: Apple’s foldable has a new crease to deal with, and it’s in buyer confidence
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority The iPhone Duo started shipping last Friday, but its release hasn’t been off to a great start. A large number of enthusiasts who paid a pretty price for the pretty new foldable found its inner screen breaking with minimal use . The damage has been so widespread — and maybe even worse was the damage to Apple’s image — that the fruit company had to publicly acknowledge the issue and confirm free replacements for anyone whose iPhone Duo broke so soon. Independent teardowns by JerryRigEverything and iFixit also confirm the screen’s poor durability , especially around the central part of the hinge. The most common image we’ve seen is a black line running from the top or bottom edge to the middle of the folding screen, with another line, often colored and thicker, forming a right angle to it.

title: The true cost of folding: What a Galaxy Z Fold 8 or iPhone Duo costs to own for a year
summary: Owning Samsung's or Apple's foldable phone can be way more expensive than the price tag will tell you.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority Paying a premium for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 or the iPhone Duo might seem justified when you consider what each phone offers. But the purchase price is only part of the story. Over the next year, accessories, potential repair bills, and depreciation can all add to the cost of ownership, making that initial price tag a less reliable indicator of what you’ll actually spend. That’s where total cost of ownership (TCO) comes in. I’ll break down the estimated cost of owning each foldable for its first year, then see how a single accident, such as a damaged screen, could tip the scales. With the Z Fold 8’s projected depreciation, the eye-watering cost of replacing the iPhone Duo’s screen , and lingering questions about durability , let’s attempt to find out which foldable will actually be cheaper to own.

title: I’ve used Google Home for 10 years, and it’s never felt so frustrating
summary: Is Google even trying?
body: Sigh. More than anything else in Google’s current product portfolio, Google Home is among the most frustrating. We’re now 10 years into Google’s smart home platform, and while it should feel mature and robust at this stage in its lifecycle, it instead has never felt more precarious . I say this as someone whose house is built around Google Home. My security cameras, thermostat, smart speakers, and smart displays are all made by Google. It’s the smart home ecosystem I chose years ago, and the one I’ve ultimately stuck with.

title: Reddit is coming for logged-out browsing, and users aren’t having it
summary: The plan isn't getting many upvotes.
body: TL;DR Reddit plans to shift to a primarily logged-in experience, potentially limiting how people browse the platform without an account. Nearly 59% of Reddit’s daily active uniques were logged out in Q3 2026, meaning the change could affect the majority of its audience. Reddit will begin testing the changes in select markets outside the US, but users are already pushing back against the idea. Reddit’s about to look and feel a lot different, and no, I’m not just talking about the new For You and Following feeds the platform announced yesterday. Reddit is planning something much bigger — something that could fundamentally change how millions access the platform. Earlier today, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman announced that the platform is transitioning to a primarily logged-in experience, and users are (very) unhappy with the development.

title: Google brings richer document editing to Gemini on mobile and the web
summary: Gemini is ready for your revision notes as its document powers expand.
body: TL;DR Gemini is bringing in-app document editing and preview to mobile and the web. After creating custom files, Gemini users can directly interact with the preview to deliver further revision requests. The mobile app supports PDFs, while Gemini on the web can handle a larger variety of file types. At this point, we’ve all seen how easy it is for AI to generate some documents . But there’s still often a big gap between getting that first draft produced, and fine-tuning the model’s output to the point where every last element is just how we want it to be. Google’s always working on tweaks to improve that process, and today the company shares some of its latest progress. Over on its news blog , Google is highlighting some of the new ways Gemini is learning to work with files like PDFs, spreadsheets, presentations, and even code. Users can now easily explain their edits to Gemini and get previews straight away, combining text and visual input to refine what Gemini creates.

title: Garmin Messenger is placing too much trust in SMS verification, and this might not end well
summary: Your old chats might not be gone when your phone number is reassigned.
body: TL;DR A Garmin Messenger user reports restoring their entire chat history on a second phone using only SMS verification, without a Garmin account password. The findings raise concerns that recycled phone numbers could let new owners access previous conversations, including sensitive location information. Garmin has reportedly been informed of the issue, but it hasn’t confirmed a fix. Handing over an old phone number shouldn’t mean handing over your private conversations. But a Garmin Messenger user has raised an uncomfortable question: Could the next person assigned your number inherit your chats, too? In a Reddit post , the user describes installing Garmin Messenger on a second, freshly set-up phone. They entered their existing number, verified an SMS code, and watched their previous conversations reappear. No Garmin account password was required. The second phone reportedly also began sending and receiving messages, with no obvious way to view or remotely disconnect other sessions.

Google Sheets is also getting compact pivot tables and improved Excel compatibility, with both features available to all users. Google Sheets already handles large amounts of data well, but add Gemini into the mix, and things get a lot more interesting. You can ask it to organize information, categorize hundreds of entries, or fill out an entire spreadsheet without doing all the tedious work yourself.
